page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-8GB is a general-purpose virtual server instance belonging to the Starter family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The hardware profile includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside 40 GB of local SSD storage. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the instance.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% tier. However, multi-core and multi-threaded performance is more constrained due to the shared CPU allocation and 2-core limit; the stress-ng multi-core score and static web serving throughput fall into the average range, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU scores register in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed, with read/write bandwidths for large blocks performing at average levels, but PassMark memory and database operations scoring in the lower tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a balanced resource density for entry-level workloads, leveraging high-performing AMD EPYC hardware at a budget-friendly tier, though resource sharing introduces potential performance variability under sustained multi-core loads. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose applications, single-threaded processing tasks, basic web serving, development environments, and small-scale testing where peak multi-core throughput is not continuously required.
